claims.statement: The Jev-optin approach remains architecturally valid: every gate stays deterministic and the adapter is injected like the executor; the change surface since the research base does not invalidate the design.
The requestDigest anchor moved from csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs:806 to :872 after the in-loop completion enforcement landed; the approach's anchor is stale.

In-loop completion enforcement (e07d84a) added evaluator contracts, loop guards, binding receipts, closure/verification status, and a supersession cursor; the never-Jev boundary must enumerate all of them.

capabilities remain csm-orchestrate-capabilities/2 and lib/capabilities.mjs hard-codes v2, so a capabilities/3 decision block requires a revision-aware loader while preserving .skills[].activation.mode for the router.
Every new schema id must be registered in root schemas/registry.json with a matching schemaContentDigest, and additive revisions need a compatibility-matrix.json pair.
The request envelope is still csm-orchestrate-request/1 with additionalProperties:false, so opt-in needs a request/2 plus a dual-accepting intake.
csm-orchestrate/decision-points.json is not packed because pack-bootstrap only copies csm-orchestrate/lib, capabilities.json, and schemas; it must be added to the pack manifest or relocated.
Tracked .agents/decisions/ requires a new AGENTS_DIR_SECTION mapping in scripts/lib/agents-index.mjs and a ## decisions/ README heading or the artifact-index gate fails.
All five Jev-relevant worktrees are already merged into main; only wt/csm-browse-daemon-flake carries uncommitted test-only edits, off the Jev surface.

Fail-open classification should use OpenRouter typed errors: 402 payment_required, 401 authentication, 403 permission_denied, 429 rate_limit_exceeded, 5xx/529 provider faults, 404 not_found; all revert to the harness model.

executiveSummary.content: Re-validation of the committed approach against main f2a654d. Research base was ba7a6ab; three commits intervene (e07d84a enforcement, 910e624 approach, f2a654d browse flake). The routing/authority design survives; the schema/capability registration mechanics and the never-Jev boundary need updating. Pipeline: intake -> delta analysis -> anchor re-verification -> per-decision/per-phase verdicts -> adaptations -> verify. All five worktrees are already merged; no merge collision is expected. The dominant risks remain call-count/latency blow-up and applying a confidently-wrong classification, both bounded by the approach's reversible-only apply set and baseline agreement.

keyFindings.content: K1 architecture still valid (supported). K2 requestDigest moved :806 -> :872 (supported). K3 never-Jev boundary must include the new enforcement surfaces (supported). K4 capabilities/3 needs a revision-aware loader (supported). K5 registry + compatibility-matrix entries required (supported). K6 request/2 + intake dual-accept required (supported). K7 decision-points.json must be packed (supported). K8 .agents/decisions/ index class required (supported). K9 worktrees already merged (partially-supported, medium). K10 fail-open uses OpenRouter typed errors (supported).

processAppendix.content: Tier: DEEP. Source mode: hybrid. Method: git delta analysis, anchor re-verification with file:line, per-decision and per-phase adversarial verdicts, worktree ancestry check. Independence: the validation was performed by a separate research subagent, not the approach author. No repo writes during research.

recommendation.content: Proceed with the approach after applying the adaptations, and build it in a wt/jev-optin worktree. Treat the never-Jev boundary as including all in-loop enforcement surfaces. Re-anchor every byte-identity test to index.mjs:872 and extend it to the /2 control records and the supersession cursor. Register request/2 and capabilities/3 before wiring the transport.

tldr.content: The Jev-optin approach is still architecturally valid but not execution-ready. Eleven concrete adaptations are needed after the in-loop completion enforcement landed (e07d84a): re-anchor requestDigest to csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs:872; add capabilities/3 plus a revision-aware loader; register every new schema id in schemas/registry.json and compatibility-matrix.json; dual-accept csm-orchestrate-request/2 in intake; pack csm-orchestrate/decision-points.json; add the .agents/decisions/ index class; extend the never-Jev boundary to evaluator contracts, loop guards, binding receipts, closure/verification status, and the supersession cursor; extend byte-identity tests to the /2 records; respect the SKILL.md line budget (build 475, deep-research 471, cap 500); reword D7 to operator-runtime-only; and build in wt/jev-optin.

unverifiedClaims.content: The claim that all worktrees are fully merged is based on an ancestry check, not a semantic review of every branch diff. The Jev layer's interaction with the run-boundary remainder evaluator was not executed; it is a design-level compatibility claim. No live Jev call was re-run in this validation pass.
